chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from ʿAbd al-Malik, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about turning in salat (prayer): does it invalidate the salat (prayer)? He said: “No, though I do not like that it be done.”

What is meant by this report is that if he does not turn to what is behind him, but only turns to the right and the left, then that does not invalidate the salat (prayer), even though it diminishes it. But if the turning is complete, then it invalidates the salat (prayer), according to what we mentioned previously.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Whoever thinks that he is in a state of taharah (ritual purity) and performs salat (prayer), then later learns that he was not in a state of taharah (ritual purity), should purify himself and repeat the salat (prayer). Likewise, whoever performs salat (prayer) in a garment thinking that it is tahir (ritually pure), then later comes to know that it was najis (ritually impure), and he had been negligent in praying in it without examining it, must repeat the salat (prayer).
We have already clarified that in the chapter of taharah (ritual purity) and explained it, and it is also supported by what he narrated:

key_terms.أَعَادَ: he repeated, indicating the obligation to perform the salat (prayer) again
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.تَطَهَّرَ: he purified himself, meaning he attained ritual purity before repeating salat (prayer)
key_terms.طَاهِرٌ: ritually pure, describing a garment believed to be clean
key_terms.طَهَارَةٍ: ritual purity required for valid salat (prayer)
key_terms.نَجِسًا: ritually impure, describing the garment later found impure

ai.seo_question: Does turning during salat (prayer) or discovering impurity afterward require repeating the prayer?
ai.summary: This passage discusses legal rulings related to salat (prayer), especially the effect of turning during prayer and praying without actual taharah (ritual purity). Slight turning to the right or left does not invalidate the salat (prayer), though it is disliked, while a complete turn invalidates it. It also states that if one later discovers lack of taharah (ritual purity) or najasah (ritual impurity) in clothing, the salat (prayer) must be repeated under the conditions described.
